Accuracy is misleading: always predicting 'no finding' gives about 88%

questions.prompt: Why did the team use a stratified train/validation/test split instead of a purely random split?
rubric_expectations: Stratification keeps the same share of positives in every subset
A random split could leave a small test set with very few positives
Otherwise the F1 estimate is unstable/unreliable

source_refs.quote: We used a stratified train/validation/test split (70/15/15) so that each subset keeps the same share of positive images as the full dataset.
